title: SPOP-mediated nuclear ubiquitination degradation of p62/SQSTM1 contributes to HR repair
task: Determine SPOP-mediated nuclear p62/SQSTM1 degradation mechanism in homologous recombination repair
key_results: SPOP-p62 interaction enhanced in nucleus upon DNA damage; SPOP ubiquitinates p62 at K7, triggering degradation and upregulating RAD51/FLNA; patient-derived p62 SBC mutations (S276Y/S277G/S277I) increase radiotherapy sensitivity via HR deficiency and reduced RAD51/γ-H2AX foci
comments: Intriguing paradox: p62 degradation enhances HR, contrasting its canonical autophagy adaptor role; the SBC mutations as radiotherapy sensitizers offer therapeutic potential but require validation in clinical cohorts.

model_io.model: Cancer cells and xenograft models with WT or mutant p62

hypotheses.hypothesis: SPOP-mediated nuclear p62 degradation enhances HR repair by stabilizing RAD51/FLNA
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: SPOP ubiquitinates p62 at K7; degradation increases RAD51/FLNA and HR efficiency

hypotheses.hypothesis: p62 SBC mutations impair SPOP binding and increase radiotherapy sensitivity
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: SBC mutations reduce SPOP-mediated degradation, decrease RAD51/FLNA, impair HR, and increase radiotherapy sensitivity in vitro/in vivo

title: A cholesterol-dependent LRRC8A-caveolin-1 axis sustains KRAS/EGFR signaling, ribosome biogenesis and growth in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma
task: Elucidate LRRC8A-caveolin-1 axis in coordinating volume homeostasis, oncogenic signaling, and ribosome biogenesis in pancreatic cancer
key_results: LRRC8A drives proliferation-associated S-phase volumetric expansion; forms cholesterol-dependent complex with CAV1; LRRC8A/CAV1 disruption suppresses KRAS/EGFR signaling, ribosome biogenesis, and protein synthesis; cholesterol depletion destabilizes LRRC8A-CAV1; LRRC8A inhibition suppresses PDO growth
comments: Integrative model linking osmotic/volumetric regulation to oncogenic signaling and biosynthesis; the mutual stabilization and cholesterol-dependency suggest membrane architecture is a rate-limiting control point.

model_io.model: PDAC cell lines, xenograft models, and patient-derived organoids

hypotheses.hypothesis: LRRC8A-CAV1 complex coordinates volume expansion with oncogenic signaling and ribosome biogenesis
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: LRRC8A/CAV1 disruption or cholesterol depletion suppresses KRAS/EGFR, ribosome biogenesis, and biosynthetic activity; PDO growth blocked

title: Fas acts as a T cell co-stimulatory receptor via both death domain-independent and -dependent mechanisms
task: Characterize Fas as a T cell co-stimulatory receptor integrating TCR signaling via death domain-independent and -dependent mechanisms
key_results: Fas constitutively localizes to immune synapse; DD-independent signaling lowers TCR activation threshold; DD-dependent cascade (FADD/caspase-8/RIPK1/TAK1) drives gene activation; caspase-8 catalytic activity is a tipping point favoring co-stimulation over death
comments: Elegant dual-mechanism model; the spatial organization at the immune synapse is key, and the switching logic between death and co-stimulation via caspase-8 inhibition is therapeutically relevant.

model_io.model: Primary T cells and antigen-presenting cells

hypotheses.hypothesis: Fas lowers TCR threshold and drives co-stimulation via both DD-independent (spatial) and DD-dependent (RIPK1/TAK1) signaling
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: Fas constitutively clusters at immune synapse; DD-independent proximity lowers threshold; caspase-8 tipping point switches from death to co-stimulation

title: ATF4 coordinates amino acid and nucleotide synthesis with selective protein translation to ensure proper DNA replication timing in leukemia cells

comments: Elegant metabolic-translational coordination mechanism; however, the selective translation mechanism and identity of the critical replication proteins beyond origin-firing machinery remain partially characterized.

model_io.model: Acute leukemia cells

hypotheses.hypothesis: ATF4 coordinates metabolic and translational programs for DNA replication fidelity in leukemia
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: ATF4 drives amino acid/nucleotide biosynthesis and selective translation of replication machinery; inhibition disrupts timing and induces differentiation

title: Soluble CD95L triggers Caspase-10-driven reactive oxygen species production in neutrophils and aggravates anti-neutrophil cytoplasmic antibody-vasculitis

comments: Clear mechanistic pathway from disease-relevant stimulus to ROS via non-apoptotic signaling offers therapeutic target; the metalloprotease-mediated CD95L shedding step could be a secondary intervention point.
